doc: The permission policy of opencode. bin/sync-harness renders `opencode` into opencode.json; plugins/harness-guard.js enforces `roles`. The person, 2026-11-24 ('ENABLE the agents'): no shell, read or edit rules; only the read-only roles are limited.

opencode.doc: tool_deny: opencode tools denied for every agent. subagent: all agent orchestration goes through T3 delegate_task (the person, 2026-11-22). tool_allow: opencode tools allowed for every agent; external_directory does not prompt (2026-11-23). skill_deny: skills no session loads.

roles.doc: Enforced by plugins/harness-guard.js in every opencode session (a T3 child runs as build, so agent frontmatter cannot limit it; 2026-11-22). A session's role is the first line `role: <name>` in its first user message (after T3's header and preamble), stored per session the first time it is seen and never relaxed. No role line: no limit. An unknown role gets unknown_role. allow and deny are action globs (opencode permission actions; MCP tools are <server>_<tool>); deny wins, and an action not allowed is denied. In a role session an ask becomes a deny: the child returns needs-answer instead. Code Mode `execute` is never evaluated as a permission, so the plugin gates it against the same allowlist; a read-only role may not use it. reviewer and advisor allow external_directory so a T3 reviewer can read its role file and the review bundle outside its worktree. implementor: everything but T3 tools and question; its context is the slim prompt.

context.doc: What an implementor session loads (the person, 2026-11-24: slim what an implementor loads; with the full harness DeepSeek used 2.5x the tokens of bare, Phase 8). The plugin's context hook replaces the agent prompt with this file's body, drops these instruction sources, and drops the global AGENTS.md block (the project's AGENTS.md stays). Only a session whose sole role is implementor.
